description: A parent must decide whether to accept a neighbor's barter proposal for weekend childcare, exchanging childcare shifts for private guitar lessons, and settle the schedule and care routine with input from the prospective sitter and a nearby parent who knows the child well.

shared_context.S1: Maya needs informal childcare for several Saturday evenings this spring and can offer beginner guitar lessons in exchange.
shared_context.S2: Jon is the only person currently being considered as the childcare provider for this arrangement. Leila is attending only to share care information from her previous time with Maya's child, not to provide childcare or negotiate a separate exchange.
shared_context.S3: Maya decides whether to accept the arrangement and states the final terms.
shared_context.S4: The proposed shifts cover dinner and evening care, so the practical schedule, exchange, and care routine need to be clear before Maya agrees.

PF1.text: Jon can provide childcare on exactly March 9, March 23, April 6, and April 20, from 17:00 to 22:00, in exchange for exactly three 45-minute guitar lessons from Maya.

PF2.text: Leila cared for Maya's child during three evening visits and found that the child settles reliably only after a 20-minute walk before dinner; Leila also knows the child's prescribed inhaler must remain in the outer pocket of the blue backpack.

decisions.caregiver: string, use Jon because he is the sole provider
decisions.childcare_dates: string, use March 9, March 23, April 6, and April 20

acceptance_conditions: The arrangement must be accepted with Jon as the sole caregiver.
Childcare must be scheduled for March 9, March 23, April 6, and April 20.
Each childcare shift must run from 17:00 to 22:00.
Maya must provide exactly three 45-minute guitar lessons in exchange.
The final care plan must include a 20-minute walk before dinner.
The child's inhaler must be confirmed as staying in the outer pocket of the blue backpack.
Leila's prior-care reference must be completed before acceptance.
The settlement must log the childcare-for-lessons exchange with Jon.
The settlement must log the care logistics learned from Leila.

content_checks.C3: decisions['childcare_hours'] == '17:00-22:00' or decisions['childcare_hours'] == '17:00 to 22:00' or decisions['childcare_hours'] == '17:00 to 22:00 (5:00 PM to 10:00 PM)'
content_checks.C9: decisions['walk_before_dinner'] == True and decisions['inhaler_location_confirmed'] == True and any(c['type'] in ['care_guideline', 'care_protocol', 'care_logistics', 'medication_safety', 'childcare'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any(c['type'] in ['childcare_exchange', 'childcare', 'childcare_schedule', 'exchange'] and c['target'] in ['Jon', 'Maya'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Jon's exact availability fixes Jon as the sole caregiver, the four childcare dates, the 17:00-22:00 hours, and the exactly three 45-minute lessons rather than leaving those terms to an unsupported guess.
Leila's firsthand care experience supplies the exact 20-minute walk, the outer-pocket blue-backpack inhaler location, and the care reference and logistics commitment needed before acceptance.
